===Etymology 1===
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:wyke<id:week>|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|wyke}}, {{m|enm|weke}}, from {{inh|en|ang|wice}}, {{m|ang|wucu|t=week}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*wikā}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*wikǭ|t=sequence; week}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*weyg-}}, {{m|ine-pro|*weyk-|t=to bend, curve}}. Related to {{m|en|weak}} and dialectal {{m+|en|wick|id=corner|t=corner}}; see {{cog|gem-pro|*wīkwaną|*wīk(w)aną|t=to bend, yield, cease}}.
{{col-top|2|cog}}
Cognate with {{cog|sco|ouk}}, {{m|sco|oulk|t=week}}, {{cog|yol|wick}}, {{m|yol|wik|t=week}}, {{cog|frr|waag}}, {{m|frr|Week}}, {{m|frr|weg|t=week}}, {{cog|stq|Wiek}}, {{m|stq|Wíek|t=week}}, {{cog|fy|wike|t=week}}, {{cog|bar|Wochn|t=week}}, {{cog|cim|boch}}, {{m|cim|bòcha|t=week}}, {{cog|nl|week|t=week}}, {{cog|de|Woche|t=week}}, {{cog|nds-de|Week|t=week}}, {{cog|li|waek}}, {{m|li|Wéëk|t=week}}, {{cog|lb|Woch|t=week}}, {{cog|mhn|boch|t=week}}, {{cog|wym|woch|t=week}}, {{cog|yi|וואָך|t=week}}, {{cog|da|uge|t=week}}, {{cog|ovd|wiku}}, {{m|ovd|wikå|t=week}}, {{cog|fo,is|vika|t=week}}, {{cog|gmq-jmk|vuku|t=week}}, {{cog|nb|uke|t=week}}, {{cog|nn|veke}}, {{m|nn|vika}}, {{m|nn|viku}}, {{m|nn|vukku}}, {{m|nn|vuku|t=week}}, {{cog|gmq-scy|uga|t=week}}, {{cog|sv|vecka|t=week}}, {{cog|got|𐍅𐌹𐌺𐍉|t=sequence; week}}; also {{cog|kw|gwigh|t=periwinkles, whelks}}, {{cog|ga|faocha}}, {{m|ga|faochóg|t=periwinkle}}, {{cog|la|vicis|t=alteration, turn; time}}, {{cog|grc|εἴκω|t=to yield}}, {{cog|sq|vig|t=bier, litter, stretcher}}, {{cog|kmr|avêtin}}, {{m|kmr|avitin}}, {{m|kmr|avîtin}}, {{m|kmr|havêtin}}, {{m|kmr|havîtin|t=to cast, hurl, throw}}, {{cog|fa|آویختَن|tr=âvixtan|t=to hang, suspend}}, {{m|fa|بیختن|tr=bēxtan / bixtan|t=to sieve, sift}}. Related also to {{cog|ang|wīcan|t=to yield, give way}}, English {{doublet|en|weak|wick|notext=1}}. 

Superseded non-native {{ncog|enm|semaigne|t=week}} borrowed from {{ncog|fro|semaine}}, {{m|fro|semeigne|t=week}}.
{{col-bottom}}

|url=http://www.economist.com/news/finance-and-economics/21580518-terrible-name-interesting-trend-rise-smart-beta|title=The rise of smart beta
|passage=Investors face a quandary. Cash offers a return of virtually zero in many developed countries; government-bond yields may have risen in recent '''weeks''' but they are still unattractive. Equities have suffered two big bear markets since 2000 and are wobbling again. It is hardly surprising that pension funds, insurers and endowments are searching for new sources of return.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170516065930/http://www.economist.com:80/news/finance-and-economics/21580518-terrible-name-interesting-trend-rise-smart-beta|archivedate=16 May 2017}}
#* {{RQ:en:CNN|author=Allison Chinchar|title=Multiday severe weather threat could continue tornado streak this week|url=https://www.cnn.com/2024/05/05/weather/severe-weather-threat-tornadoes-midwest|date=2024-05-05|passage=Some of the same areas hit by tornadoes just a little over a '''week''' ago are expecting severe storms again Monday afternoon and evening.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20240515060056/https://www.cnn.com/2024/05/05/weather/severe-weather-threat-tornadoes-midwest/}}
# A period of seven days beginning with [[Sunday]] or [[Monday]].
# A period of five days beginning with [[Monday]].
# A subdivision of the [[month]] into longer periods of work days punctuated by shorter [[weekend]] periods of days for markets, rest, or religious observation such as a [[sabbath]].
#: {{ux|en|A 4-day '''week''' consists of Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday.}}
# {{lb|en|following a named day}} A date seven days after ({{n-g|sometimes}} before) the specified day.
#: {{ux|en|I'll see you Thursday '''week'''. ''[''a week on Thursday, i.e. Thursday after next'']''}}
#: {{ux|en|The wedding is tomorrow '''week'''. ''[''a week tomorrow, i.e. in eight days' time'']''}}
